# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# This comment is for the user.
# The base image ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm
# already contains OpenMPI, Flux, and necessary libraries (like libfabric with EFA provider)
# pre-configured for multi-node execution on AWS. This Dockerfile builds the
# OSU Micro-Benchmarks on top of that established environment.

# Set OSU benchmarks version for consistency
ENV OSU_VERSION=7.3

# Build and install the OSU Micro-Benchmarks
# A single RUN command is used to reduce image layers.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    wget \
    automake \
    autoconf \
    ca-certificates && \
    # Download, extract, and change into the source directory
    cd /tmp && \
    wget "https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/download/mvapich/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    tar -xvf "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    cd "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}" && \
    # FIX: Configure with an install prefix to define the installation path.
    # This prepares for a standard autotools installation.
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --prefix=/usr/local && \
    # Compile the benchmarks
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # FIX: Use 'make install' for a robust and standard installation.
    # This correctly places executables onto the system PATH.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build artifacts and source code to keep the image lean
    cd / && \
    rm -rf "/tmp/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}" "/tmp/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    # Clean up apt cache
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a default command to demonstrate that a benchmark is available and on the PATH
CMD ["osu_latency", "--help"]

# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# This comment is for the user.
# The base image ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm
# already contains OpenMPI, Flux, and necessary libraries (like libfabric with EFA provider)
# pre-configured for multi-node execution on AWS. This Dockerfile builds the
# OSU Micro-Benchmarks on top of that established environment.

# Set OSU benchmarks version for consistency
ENV OSU_VERSION=7.3

# Build and install the OSU Micro-Benchmarks
# A single RUN command is used to reduce image layers.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    wget \
    automake \
    autoconf \
    ca-certificates && \
    # Download, extract, and change into the source directory
    cd /tmp && \
    wget "https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/download/mvapich/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    tar -xvf "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    cd "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}" && \
    # Configure the build to use the MPI compilers provided by the base image
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx && \
    # Compile the benchmarks

    # Clean up the build artifacts and source code to keep the image lean
    cd / && \
    rm -rf "/tmp/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}" "/tmp/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \

    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

CMD ["osu_latency", "--help"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the OSU Latency benchmark
# across two AWS ARM-based CPU instances in a Kubernetes cluster,
# utilizing AWS EFA for high-performance networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: osu-latency-aws-cpu
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job.
  # Set to 2 to run the benchmark across two nodes.
  size: 2
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # OSU Latency is a point-to-point benchmark requiring 2 tasks.
  tasks: 2

  # Do not delete pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod-level settings that apply to all pods created by this MiniCluster.
  pod:
    # Resources requested for the entire pod.
    # This is required to attach an AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to each pod.
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Flux Operator specific settings
  flux:
    # Set the architecture for the flux-view container, required for AWS ARM instances (e.g., Graviton).
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use an ARM-compatible image for the Flux sidecar container.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Per instructions, disable the automatic injection of the flux-view sidecar.
      # Note: This requires the main application container to have flux binaries pre-installed.
      disable: true

  # Logging configuration
  logging:
    # Fail the job on any logging configuration error.
    strict: true

  # Define the main application container. Only one container is allowed.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-latency
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator prepends 'flux run -n <tasks>'.
      # 'osu_latency' is the executable for the OSU Latency benchmark.
      command: osu_latency
      # Ensure the latest version of the container image is always pulled.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # This container is the application workload, not a launcher. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: osu-latency-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: /usr/local/bin/osu_latency
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-latency
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 2
  tasks: 2

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Build the OSU benchmarks. You MUST have MPI support enabled. You MUST ensure osu_latency is on the path.
You MUST build for a multi-node MPI environment

context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3).
context.details:
Run The OSU Latency benchmark across 2 nodes.
You MUST run on 2 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
